findings.title: Absent drain-timeout form field silently resets configured value to 60.0
findings.problem: safe_float(form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"), 60.0, ...) returns the hardcoded 60.0 whenever the form key is missing. triggarr/templates/settings.html currently renders no input named shutdown_drain_timeout (grep finds request_timeout at line 53 and max_consecutive_failures at line 74, but no drain input; the template task is a separate, not-yet-applied step of plan 75-02). So any settings save from the live UI overwrites a user's persisted drain timeout with 60.0. The adjacent tracking_delay_seconds field — also not rendered in the form — deliberately uses current_settings.general.tracking_delay_seconds instead of a literal default, which is the established pattern for a non-rendered general field. pending: confirm the settings.html drain input lands before this handler ships; if it does, the exposure narrows to non-browser/partial POSTs.
findings.fix_hint: use current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the safe_float default instead of the literal 60.0, so an absent form field preserves the persisted value (matching the tracking_delay_seconds pattern)
findings.why_it_matters: A user who set a 300s drain timeout in triggarr.toml loses it to 60.0 the next time anyone saves any unrelated setting from the UI, shortening graceful shutdown without warning.

findings.title: Persisted shutdown_drain_timeout is inert — scheduler still reads the import-time env constant
findings.problem: This diff completes the write half of the drain-timeout config loop (GET render var + POST safe_float parse -> validated SettingsModel -> atomic TOML write), but nothing reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown. I read triggarr/search/scheduler.py: the drain still uses the module-level constant `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT: float = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()` (scheduler.py:81), computed at IMPORT time from `os.environ['TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT']` only (scheduler.py:58-74, no `configured` parameter). All five consumption sites — the two INFO drain-entry logs (scheduler.py:611, 618), `asyncio.timeout(_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT)` (scheduler.py:634), and the two WARNING timeout logs (scheduler.py:648, 656) — reference that constant. A user who sets 120.5 in Settings gets a 303, sees the value persisted and re-rendered on the next GET, and still drains at 60.0s. This is a silent no-op knob: the UI affirmatively lies about behavior. The wiring is scoped to plan 75-03 (.planning/phases/75-drain-timeout-config-parity-deferred-record-correction/75-03-PLAN.md D-04/D-05: target signature `_read_shutdown_drain_timeout(configured: float = 60.0)` plus reading `app.state.settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout` in the shutdown block), which has NOT landed — so this is a wave-ordering exposure, not a design defect, but it is user-visible if 75-02 ships without 75-03.
findings.fix_hint: Ship 75-03 in the same release as 75-02 — refactor _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take a `configured` default and resolve it from app.state.settings at shutdown time, replacing the import-time _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT constant in the drain block.
findings.why_it_matters: The drain protects in-flight Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr search cycles from an abrupt SIGKILL. An operator who raises the timeout because their cycles legitimately take longer than 60s will believe they are protected and still lose in-flight cycles at 60s. The failure is invisible until a shutdown races a long cycle.

findings.title: settings.html has no drain-timeout input — GET render var is orphaned and its own test fails RED
findings.problem: routes.py:446 adds "shutdown_drain_timeout": settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout to the settings_page render context, but grep -c shutdown_drain_timeout triggarr/templates/settings.html returns 0 — the template renders no matching input. The context key is dead, and the field is unreachable from the UI: the POST parse at routes.py:550 will only ever see form.get(...) is None and fall back to the 60.0 default on every real browser save. Worse, this SILENTLY RESETS a TOML-configured value: a user who hand-edits shutdown_drain_timeout = 300.0 into triggarr.toml and then saves any unrelated setting from the UI has it overwritten back to 60.0, because the handler rebuilds the whole [general] block from form data (unlike tracking_delay_seconds at routes.py:549, which is deliberately carried over from current_settings precisely because it has no form input). I confirmed the gap empirically: uv run pytest tests/test_web.py -k "drain_timeout or new_config_fields" gives 1 failed, 2 passed — test_settings_page_renders_new_config_fields fails at tests/test_web.py:694 asserting "shutdown_drain_timeout" in response.text. The two round-trip tests pass only because they POST the field directly, bypassing the missing template. Plan 75-02 lists triggarr/templates/settings.html in files_modified with must-have D-02 (numeric input) and D-10 (env-override precedence help text); neither landed. HEAD is the RED commit ce567d3 ("test(75-02): add failing drain-timeout settings round-trip test") with routes.py uncommitted, so this is mid-TDD — the template task is simply not yet done.

findings.title: Saved drain timeout never affects shutdown
findings.problem: POSTing 120.5 persists the value, but scheduler.py still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, initialized exclusively from the environment with a 60-second default. Even after restart, the saved setting is ignored. Operators extending the drain window still get resources forcibly closed after 60 seconds while work may remain active.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators extending the drain window still get resources forcibly closed after 60 seconds while work may remain active.
findings.fix_hint: Resolve the timeout from app.state.settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown, with the intended environment override, and test that a saved value controls the actual drain.

findings.title: Settings form cannot submit the new value
findings.problem: settings.html contains no shutdown_drain_timeout input. Adding template context alone does not expose it, so ordinary browser saves always submit a missing value and persist 60.0. A value saved through a direct POST cannot survive the next UI save. The existing rendering test explicitly expects this missing input.
findings.why_it_matters: Ordinary browser saves submit a missing value and persist 60.0, so a value saved through a direct POST cannot survive the next UI save.
findings.fix_hint: Add a numeric input associated with settings-form, supporting fractional values and matching bounds. Preserve the current value when the field is absent, and verify a GET-to-POST round trip.
